title: Why Custom Training Loops? 🧐
description: Compare model.fit with manual loops, and learn when you need full control.

slides.title: model.fit() is Awesome, But... 🚀
slides.content:
# The Built‑in Training Loop

`model.fit()` handles:
- Batching, shuffling
- Forward pass
- Loss computation
- Backpropagation
- Metric tracking
- Callbacks

It's perfect for 90% of cases. But sometimes you need **more control**.

slides.title: When You Need Custom Loops 🛠️
slides.content:
# Scenarios

- **Multiple models interacting** (GANs: generator + discriminator).
- **Non‑standard loss** with extra tensors or regularisation.
- **Custom gradient manipulation** (gradient clipping, adding noise).
- **Research**: trying new optimisation algorithms or training dynamics.
- **Meta‑learning**: updating weights in inner/outer loops.

> Analogy: `model.fit()` is driving an automatic car. Custom loops = manual transmission – more control, but you need to know what you're doing.

quizData.question: Which of the following is NOT a good reason to write a custom training loop?

options.text: Implementing a GAN with alternating updates
Simple image classification with standard cross‑entropy
Adding a gradient penalty to the loss
Training a model with reinforcement learning

quizData.explanation: For a standard supervised task, `model.fit()` is sufficient and easier. Custom loops are for non‑standard requirements.

slides.title: The Core Components of a Training Loop
slides.content: Any loop must do these five things:
slides.codeSnippet:
# Pseudocode of a custom loop
for epoch in range(epochs):
    for batch in dataset:
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            predictions = model(batch_x, training=True)
            loss = loss_fn(batch_y, predictions)
        grads = tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_variables)
        optimizer.apply_gradients(zip(grads, model.trainable_variables))

slides.title: Still Use Keras Components 💡
slides.content: Custom loops don't mean ditching Keras! You still use `tf.keras.layers`, `tf.keras.optimizers`, `tf.keras.losses`, and `tf.keras.metrics`. Just the orchestration is manual.
